Missing newline at end of file with multiple array of tables can corrupt during dumping
Missing newline at end of file with multiple array of tables can corrupt during dumping

When creating a pipeline using pipenv, the Pipfile would get corrupted in certain cases: when there are multiple entries in an array of tables and the last one is at the end of the file AND does not have a final newline.

```python
import tomlkit

toml_str = '''[[products]]
name = "Hammer"

[foo]

[bar]

[[products]]
name = "Nail"'''

parsed = tomlkit.loads(toml_str)
print(tomlkit.dumps(parsed))
```

Wrong output:

```
[[products]]
name = "Hammer"

[[products]]
name = "Nail"[foo]

[bar]
```

The dumped output is no longer valid TOML — re-parsing it raises `UnexpectedCharError: Unexpected character: '['`. The tables after the last array-of-tables entry get glued onto the previous line.

Repo version: tomlkit 0.13.0. Reproduction test file: tests/test_real_issues_411_377_381.py::test_issue_381_parse_aot_without_ending_newline_roundtrip

def test_issue_411_dump_nested_dotted_table():
    # https://github.com/python-poetry/tomlkit/issues/411
    # dumps() of a sub-table loses one nesting level.
    a = tomlkit.parse("a.b.c.d='e'")["a"]
    assert a == {"b": {"c": {"d": "e"}}}
    assert dumps(a) == "b.c.d='e'"


def test_issue_411_dump_nested_dotted_table_two_levels():
    doc = tomlkit.parse("a.b.c = 1\na.b.d = 2\n")
    sub = doc["a"]["b"]
    assert sub == {"c": 1, "d": 2}
    out = dumps(sub)
    assert out == "c = 1\nd = 2\n"


def test_issue_411_dumps_accepts_table_instance():
    # dumps() should accept a Table/InlineTable directly without
    # re-wrapping it into a plain dict (which loses style and nesting).
    doc = tomlkit.parse("[a]\nb = 1\n")
    table = doc["a"]
    assert isinstance(table, Table)
    assert dumps(table) == "b = 1\n"


def test_issue_377_no_empty_parent_header_for_super_table():
    # https://github.com/python-poetry/tomlkit/issues/377
    # Adding a second sub-table should not produce an empty parent header.
    doc = tomlkit.document()

    def add_table(parent, name):
        parent.add(name, tomlkit.table())
        return parent[name]

    root = add_table(doc, "root")
    add_table(root, "first")
    add_table(root, "second")

    out = dumps(doc)
    assert "[root]\n" not in out
    assert "[root.first]" in out
    assert "[root.second]" in out


def test_issue_381_parse_aot_without_ending_newline_roundtrip():
    # https://github.com/python-poetry/tomlkit/issues/381
    # Dumping a parsed doc whose last AOT entry lacks a trailing newline
    # must not corrupt the output.
    content = (

    # The dumped output must still be parseable and preserve the data.
    reparsed = tomlkit.parse(out)

```python
[bar]
```

Missing newline at end of file with multiple array of tables can corrupt during dumping

When creating a pipeline using pipenv, the Pipfile would get corrupted in certain cases: when there are multiple entries in an array of tables and the last one is at the end of the file AND does not have a final newline.

```python
import tomlkit

toml_str = '''[[products]]
name = "Hammer"

[foo]

[bar]

[[products]]
name = "Nail"'''

parsed = tomlkit.loads(toml_str)
print(tomlkit.dumps(parsed))
```

Wrong output:

```
[[products]]
name = "Hammer"

[[products]]
name = "Nail"[foo]

[bar]
```

The dumped output is no longer valid TOML — re-parsing it raises `UnexpectedCharError: Unexpected character: '['`. The tables after the last array-of-tables entry get glued onto the previous line.

Missing newline at end of file with multiple array of tables can corrupt during dumping

When creating a pipeline using pipenv, the Pipfile would get corrupted in certain cases: when there are multiple entries in an array of tables and the last one is at the end of the file AND does not have a final newline.

```python
import tomlkit

toml_str = '''[[products]]
name = "Hammer"

[foo]

[bar]

[[products]]
name = "Nail"'''

parsed = tomlkit.loads(toml_str)
print(tomlkit.dumps(parsed))
```

Wrong output:

```
[[products]]
name = "Hammer"

[[products]]
name = "Nail"[foo]

[bar]
```

The dumped output is no longer valid TOML — re-parsing it raises `UnexpectedCharError: Unexpected character: '['`. The tables after the last array-of-tables entry get glued onto the previous line.

Repo version: tomlkit 0.13.0. Reproduction test file: tests/test_real_issues_411_377_381.py::test_issue_381_parse_aot_without_ending_newline_roundtrip

state_snapshot.issue_summary:
Missing newline at end of file with multiple array of tables can corrupt during dumping
Missing newline at end of file with multiple array of tables can corrupt during dumping

When creating a pipeline using pipenv, the Pipfile would get corrupted in certain cases: when there are multiple entries in an array of tables and the last one is at the end of the file AND does not have a final newline.

```python
import tomlkit

toml_str = '''[[products]]
name = "Hammer"

[foo]

[bar]

[[products]]
name = "Nail"'''

parsed = tomlkit.loads(toml_str)
print(tomlkit.dumps(parsed))
```

Wrong output:

```
[[products]]
name = "Hammer"

[[products]]
name = "Nail"[foo]

[bar]
```

The dumped output is no longer valid TOML — re-parsing it raises `UnexpectedCharError: Unexpected character: '['`. The tables after the last array-of-tables entry get glued onto the previous line.

Repo version: tomlkit 0.13.0. Reproduction test file: tests/test_real_issues_411_377_381.py::test_issue_381_parse_aot_without_ending_newline_roundtrip

```python
import tomlkit
```

Missing newline at end of file with multiple array of tables can corrupt during dumping

When creating a pipeline using pipenv, the Pipfile would get corrupted in certain cases: when there are multiple entries in an array of tables and the last one is at the end of the file AND does not have a final newline.

```python
import tomlkit

toml_str = '''[[products]]
name = "Hammer"

[foo]

[bar]

[[products]]
name = "Nail"'''

parsed = tomlkit.loads(toml_str)
print(tomlkit.dumps(parsed))
```

Wrong output:

```
[[products]]
name = "Hammer"

[[products]]
name = "Nail"[foo]

[bar]
```

The dumped output is no longer valid TOML — re-parsing it raises `UnexpectedCharError: Unexpected character: '['`. The tables after the last array-of-tables entry get glued onto the previous line.

Repo version: tomlkit 0.13.0. Reproduction test file: tests/test_real_issues_411_377_381.py::test_issue_381_parse_aot_without_ending_newline_roundtrip

```python
import tomlkit

toml_str = '''[[products]]
name = "Hammer"

[foo]

[bar]

[[products]]
name = "Nail"'''

parsed = tomlkit.loads(toml_str)
print(tomlkit.dumps(parsed))
```

Wrong output:

```
[[products]]
name = "Hammer"

[[products]]
name = "Nail"[foo]

[bar]
```

```python
import tomlkit

name = "Hammer"

[foo]

[bar]

[[products]]
name = "Nail"'''

```

```
[[products]]
name = "Hammer"

[[products]]
name = "Nail"[foo]

[bar]
```

```python
import tomlkit

toml_str = '''[[products]]
name = "Hammer"

[foo]

[bar]

[[products]]
name = "Nail"'''

parsed = tomlkit.loads(toml_str)
print(tomlkit.dumps(parsed))
```

Wrong output:

```
[[products]]
name = "Hammer"

[[products]]
name = "Nail"[foo]

[bar]
```

The dumped output is no longer valid TOML — re-parsing it raises `UnexpectedCharError: Unexpected character: '['`. The tables after the last array-of-tables entry get glued onto the previous line.

Missing newline at end of file with multiple array of tables can corrupt during dumping

When creating a pipeline using pipenv, the Pipfile would get corrupted in certain cases: when there are multiple entries in an array of tables and the last one is at the end of the file AND does not have a final newline.

```python
import tomlkit

toml_str = '''[[products]]
name = "Hammer"

[foo]

[bar]

[[products]]
name = "Nail"'''

parsed = tomlkit.loads(toml_str)
print(tomlkit.dumps(parsed))
```

Wrong output:

```
[[products]]
name = "Hammer"

[[products]]
name = "Nail"[foo]

[bar]
```

The dumped output is no longer valid TOML — re-parsing it raises `UnexpectedCharError: Unexpected character: '['`. The tables after the last array-of-tables entry get glued onto the previous line.

Repo version: tomlkit 0.13.0. Reproduction test file: tests/test_real_issues_411_377_381.py::test_issue_381_parse_aot_without_ending_newline_roundtrip

hypotheses: Let me look at the parser's trail handling at EOF to understand what trail value the last AoT table gets.
Let me check the changelog and see if there's a hint about the upstream fix.

Root cause confirmed: `_render_aot_table` doesn't append a newline when the table's `trivia.trail` lacks one (which is exactly what the parser produces for a final AoT entry at EOF). `_render_table` already handles this via `newline_in_table_trivia`; the AoT counterpart lacks it. Applying the minimal fix:

My fix targeted the header's trail, but the header trail is `"\n"`. The actual missing newline is on the AoT table's *last key-value* item. Let me inspect the parser's AoT handling and the trivia assignment.
The header trail is `"\n"`; the missing newline is on the last key-value of the AoT table's body. Let me check existing tests that assert exact dump output for AoT to avoid regressions.
Let me revert my ineffective patch and examine existing round-trip tests that assert exact output.
Let me check the vendored toml-test valid AoT cases for whether any lack a trailing newline.

Root cause: when the source's final AoT entry lacks a trailing newline, its last key-value item has no trailing newline, so the AoT renders glued to the next table. Since AoT entries are consolidated/reordered, this missing newline ends up mid-document. The AoT rendering must guarantee a trailing newline. Let me patch `_render_aot`.

```python
import tomlkit

toml_str = '''[[products]]
name = "Hammer"

[foo]

[bar]

[[products]]
name = "Nail"'''

```

```
[[products]]
name = "Hammer"

[[products]]
name = "Nail"[foo]

[bar]
```
